title: Cryopreservation of Mucosal Biopsies
author: Sean M. Hughes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p5adq2e

steps.title: Prepare cryopreservation medium
steps.instruction: Mix fetal bovine serum with dimethylsulfoxide to obtain a final concentration of 10% DMSO in FBS (volumes not specified).

steps.title: Chill medium at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place the prepared cryopreservation medium at 4 °C for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Aliquot medium into cryovials
steps.instruction: Dispense 0.2 mL of the chilled cryopreservation medium into each cryovial; for multiple biopsies you may use larger volumes (e.g., 1 mL for 5–10 biopsies).

steps.title: Add biopsies to cryovials
steps.instruction: Place one or more mucosal biopsies into each cryovial and ensure they are completely covered by the medium, adding more medium if necessary.

steps.title: Freeze vials to –80 °C
steps.instruction: Seal the cryovials, place them in a Mr. Frosty (or any controlled‑rate cooling device that cools at ~1 °C per minute), and freeze to –80 °C overnight.

steps.title: Store vials in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen cryovials to a liquid‑nitrogen freezer for long‑term storage until needed.

steps.title: Prepare culture medium
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of the cell‑culture medium of interest to a suitable plate or well.

steps.title: Retrieve vials from liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Remove the cryovials from the liquid‑nitrogen freezer, keeping them on a pan of liquid nitrogen until ready to thaw.

steps.title: Thaw vials in 37 °C water bath
steps.instruction: Place the cryovials in a 37 °C water bath and agitate gently until completely thawed.

steps.title: Transfer biopsies to culture medium
steps.instruction: Using forceps, move the thawed biopsies into 5 mL of room‑temperature culture medium.

steps.title: Incubate biopsies at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate the biopsies in the medium for 10 minutes at room temperature.
